newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EMU REPORT - KEY FINDINGS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EMU REPORT - KEY FINDINGS.

text.p: Following are key findings of a report on the pros and cons for the Finnish economy of membership of European economic and monetary union, and of remaining outside:
* Joining the single currency among the first would give Finland the possibility to affect decision-making regarding monetary union,
* Remaining outside would offer the possibility to collect information and learn from the experience of others how monetary union works before participating,
* The single currency will bring clear efficiency gains through lower exchange rate-related costs, increased trade and competition, and better allocation of capital,
* It is undisputable that the efficiency gains of monetary union will exceed the direct costs of implementing the single currency,
* The effects on economic stability of monetary union are contradictory,
* If the European central bank (ECB) succeeds to maintain a more credible monetary policy than a small national central bank inflation will be on average lower and steadier,
* If real interest rates fall as a result, the economic benefits will be significant over time,
* The successful implementation of monetary union can bring steadier growth than experienced in Finland during past decades,
* But external disturbances, the size and timing of which may affect Finland in different ways than other EMU countries, must be taken into consideration,
* With a common monetary policy, the exchange rate of the euro will not react to country-specific asymmetrical shocks,
* With a floating national currency the effects of such disturbances can be dampened,
* In Finland's case, asymmetrical disturbances pose the most significant problem in monetary union,
* The Finnish economy has fluctuated in a different pattern than Germany, France and other core-EU countries,

* Finland has moderately good conditions to conduct a fiscal policy smoothing out economic fluctuations also in conditions of monetary union providing that growth remains quite strong and that agreed budget savings and the Finnish convergence programme are implemented,
* The excessive deficit sanctions in the budget stability pact are unlikely to affect Finland,

* A possible problem at the start of monetary union is that many founding members will have budget deficit to GDP ratios near the three percent ceiling and their fiscal policy will not have sufficient leeway if the economic cycle turned weaker,
* The alternatives to joining EMU are either to become part of ERM-2 or to live with a floating national currency,
* ERM-2 would largely be an interim solution before membership of EMU with irrevocably locked exchange rates,
* With a floating currency, Finland will not, over time, be able to diverge much from the economic policy in other countries,
* In all scenarios, Finland must adjust to permanently low inflation, sustained public sector finances and sufficient labour cost flexibility,
* High unemployment is a topical problem in Finland and efforts to reduce unemployment should have priority in all economic policy scenarios,
* None of the EMU options at hand will by themselves solve Finland's unemployment problem,
* The necessary adjustment in real labour costs must take place, inside or outside monetary union, through greater flexibility in nominal labour costs,

* In case of a severe recession, a floating currency offers a quick mechanism to adjust real wages which does not exist inside monetary union, where it must be replaced by a rapid agreement to attack nominal labour costs,
* Although such a situation is unlikely, a national system to cope with one is needed and there is reason to be aware in advance of the measures required.

The report was compiled by a government-appointed expert group chaired by economics professor Jukka Pekkarinen. The group submitted its report to Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen on Tuesday. --Hki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, news@reuters.fi
